slides.title: SpectraTac: A Compact Camera-Free Optical Tactile Sensor with Distributed Color Sensing
slides.highlight: SpectraTac utilizes distributed color sensing and RGB illumination to estimate 3D force and contact regions without the need for cameras or high-dimensional image processing.

card.one_liner: SpectraTac is a compact, camera-free optical tactile sensor using distributed color sensing for 3D force estimation.
card.key_idea: Combines active RGB illumination with three distributed RGBC sensors in a PDMS layer, using a ResMLP framework to decode spatio-spectral features into force and contact region data.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 6-axis F/T reference; achieved 3D force MAEs (0.161-0.429 N) and 99.9% contact-region accuracy. Results appear trustworthy via real-time tracking and interactive tasks.
card.limitation: Future work is needed to improve spatial resolution, force decoupling, dynamic perception, and long-term robustness.

slides.title: N0-Foundation: Towards the Age of Tactile Intelligence
slides.highlight: This work introduces a visuo-tactile representation model and large-scale dataset to improve physical contact state perception, supporting HyECHO's goal of multimodal social perception in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: A comprehensive tactile-centric foundation for embodied manipulation integrating hardware, large-scale data, and unified representations.
card.key_idea: NeoForce learns hardware-agnostic tactile representations by using dense three-axis force fields as unified supervision across diverse visuo-tactile sensors and embodiments.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using the NeoReal (real-world) and NeoSim (simulated) suites; results show policies benefit from physical contact states over device-specific signals.

slides.title: TacForcing: Streaming Action Generation with Execution-Time Tactile Feedback
slides.tldr: STREAMING ACTION GENERATION WITH TACTILE FEEDBACK
slides.highlight: TacForcing introduces a streaming action-generation framework and Execution-Aware Tactile Attention to incorporate real-time tactile feedback into contact-rich manipulation without needing separate reactive controllers.

card.one_liner: TacForcing enables contact-rich manipulation by streaming action generation conditioned on real-time tactile feedback.
card.key_idea: A Streaming Action Expert generates action blocks progressively, using Execution-Aware Tactile Attention (EATA) to align the latest tactile updates only with the next scheduled action block.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on six UniVTAC simulation tasks (65% avg success) and three real-world tasks (69% avg success) against vision-only and tactile-reactive baselines.

slides.title: GRAFT: Grounded and Efficient Online Reinforcement Adaptation for Fine-Grained Robot Manipulation
slides.tldr: EFFICIENT ONLINE VLA ADAPTATION FOR ROBOT MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: GRAFT enables efficient online adaptation of vision-language-action policies for fine-grained tasks using grounded perception, supporting the RwB goal of embodied learning.

card.one_liner: GRAFT enables efficient online VLA adaptation for fine-grained robot manipulation using grounded perception.
card.key_idea: Uses view-specific visual anchors trained with identity-free multi-region supervision and accelerates learning via frozen-prefix KV caching and single-step action generation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on four biomedical tasks using a 45-minute budget; GRAFT achieved 82.5% success vs 57.5% for GRAFT-Union. Results appear trustworthy via controlled ablations.
card.limitation: The policy is reactive and lacks temporal context, potentially hindering performance on long-horizon tasks with changing visual targets.

slides.title: VISTA: Visually Inferred Spatial ConTact Attention for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.tldr: VISUALLY INFERRED CONTACT FEEDBACK FOR MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: VISTA-Policy uses a Visual Deformation Field to provide high-dimensional visuo-physical feedback for contact-rich tasks without requiring dedicated tactile sensors.

card.one_liner: VISTA enables contact-rich robot manipulation by using external cameras to infer gripper deformation as tactile feedback.
card.key_idea: A framework extracting a 3D Visual Deformation Field (VDF) from a compliant gripper, using energy-based denoising and a relative incremental action space for adaptive control.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on grasping, unscrewing, and calligraphy tasks against DP3 and tactile baselines; showed superior success rates, sample efficiency, and OOD scale generalization.
card.limitation: Requires the use of a compliant gripper whose structural deformation remains observable from an external camera.

slides.title: Anomaly Detection on Small Industrial Components via Vision-Based Tactile Sensing
slides.tldr: TACTILE ANOMALY DETECTION FOR INDUSTRIAL COMPONENTS
slides.highlight: This research explores vision-based tactile sensing for detecting geometry-driven defects in small components, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal perception.

card.one_liner: Evaluates unsupervised anomaly detection on small industrial components using vision-based tactile sensing for geometric defect detection.
card.key_idea: Benchmarked four feature-embedding methods (SPADE, PaDiM, FAPM, InReaCh) using a GelSight Mini sensor, focusing on nominal sample requirements, cross-position generalization, and image resolution impacts.
card.evaluation: Tested on five real industrial components using AUROC, AUPRC, and AUC-PRO@0.01. Results show SPADE leads in LR localization, while FAPM excels in HR.
card.limitation: Dataset is not publicly released due to industrial confidentiality; soft-interface gel wear limits the number of possible contact acquisitions.

slides.title: Aero Hand Open: A Simulation-Ready Tendon-Driven Hand for Dexterous Manipulation Learning
slides.tldr: SIMULATION-READY TENDON-DRIVEN HAND FOR DEXTEROUS MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a tendon-driven anthropomorphic hand with a simulation model and actuation map that allow policies to be trained in simulation and deployed without fine-tuning.

card.one_liner: A low-cost, 3D-printed tendon-driven anthropomorphic hand designed for zero-shot sim-to-real reinforcement learning transfer.
card.key_idea: Combines a MuJoCo simulation model of cable transmissions with an identified linear actuation map to connect motor commands to joint states.
card.evaluation: Validated by executing all 33 GRASP taxonomy grasp types and demonstrating in-hand cube rotation using RL policies trained in simulation.
card.limitation: The hand is deliberately underactuated, meaning joints driven by the same cable cannot be independently commanded.

slides.title: DeicticVLA: Unifying Instruction Modes Based on Language and Deictic Gestures in a Single VLA
slides.tldr: UNIFIED VLA FOR LANGUAGE AND DEICTIC GESTURE INSTRUCTIONS
slides.highlight: DeicticVLA enables a single model to handle language, vision-language, and visual instructions by canonicalizing them into text prompts and deictic masks. This approach significantly improves success rates for unseen categories and novel objects compared to language-only instructions.

card.one_liner: DeicticVLA unifies language, vision-language, and visual-only instructions into a single VLA using deictic masks.
card.key_idea: Canonicalizes three instruction modes into text prompts and SAM 2-generated deictic masks, comparing RGB visual prompting and separate-channel mask prompting with two-stage training.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on LIBERO simulation and three real-world tasks; VP-BBox and MP-Late showed strongest zero-shot generalization to unseen layouts.
